page: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-800s-amd belongs to the Optimized Cloud Compute family and provides a memory-dense hardware configuration. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs sourced from 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, supporting simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. System architecture is x86_64, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Modern vector and cryptographic execution flags are enabled, including AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16), AES, and SHA-NI. The server provides 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Storage is bundled directly via an integrated 800 GB local NVMe SSD, and one complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned. No GPU accelerator is present.

Benchmark evaluation reflects prominent single-thread capacity combined with solid memory bandwidth. In stress-ng single-core tests, the instance records top-tier results, complementing strong large-block uncached memory write throughput at 115.6 GB/sec and strong single-threaded gzip compression. General processing metrics, including Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU ratings, position the server within average industry tiers. Conversely, tests measuring multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and static web serving throughput show weaker relative figures. CPU-driven LLM inference performance drops notably on larger models such as 7B parameter architectures, indicating that compute scale is restricted by the 4-vCPU envelope despite strong individual core execution.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the instance provides high RAM density relative to its core count alongside sizable local NVMe capacity without requiring separate block volume attachments. This configuration makes it an effective choice for memory-intensive applications that require fast local disk caching rather than high core parallelism. Primary operational fits include in-memory data stores such as Redis, moderate relational databases, ETL batch staging, and application runtimes with demanding per-process memory footprints.
description: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-800s-amd is a memory-oriented server in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes a bundled 800 GB local NVMe solid-state drive along with one complimentary public IPv4 address. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, SHA-NI, and AES encryption support. Synthetic testing demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU throughput and strong large-block memory write bandwidth, alongside solid single-threaded compression performance. However, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and static web serving throughput show lower relative benchmark rankings. The high memory capacity per core combined with integrated fast local storage offers balanced resource density without external drive attachments. It is functionally configured for in-memory caching systems, intermediate data pipelines, microservices requiring elevated RAM footprints, and localized development databases.
